records.issue_text: Denial cache is written but never invalidated on permission changes, so a granted permission can be denied for up to the full TTL
records.rationale:

- It short-circuits to `Allowed: false` if the key is present (`if _, ok := s.permDenialCache.Get(...); ok { ... return &authzv1.CheckResponse{Allowed: false}, nil }`).
- It is written on any computed denial (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true) }`).

records.rationale: In `Service.List`, any error from `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` is treated as a cache miss: `if err == nil { ... } else { ... permissions, err = s.getIdentityPermissions(...) }` (service.go). records.stripped_text: Real DB errors from GetUserIdentifiers are silently retried as cache misses in the List path, doubling query load and masking the first error

records.issue_text: Denial cache key omits identity type, so user and serviceaccount subjects with the same UID string share userPermDenialCacheKey and cross-contaminate denial decisions
records.rationale: `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` does not include `IdentityType` (added in `Check` via `checkReq.IdentityType`), and `Check` builds the key as `userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, checkReq.Action, checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)` without any identity-type discriminator. This means two different subject types (e.g., user vs service account) that share the same `UserUID` string in the same namespace/action/resource could hit the same denial-cache entry and incorrectly reuse a denial decision.
records.stripped_text: Denial cache key omits identity type, so user and serviceaccount subjects with the same UID string share userPermDenialCacheKey and cross-contaminate denial decisions

records.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the denial cache key is constructed with `checkReq.ParentFolder` (`permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(..., checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)`), and `userPermDenialCacheKey` concatenates `name` and `parent` directly into the key (`... + "_" + name + "_" + parent`). records.issue_text: Deletion of the only test asserting getUserPermissions returns cached entries leaves the function's cache contract untested
records.rationale: The diff shows `getUserPermissions` no longer has a cache-read contract to test. Its cache lookup was removed (deleted block `if cached, ok := s.permCache.Get(...); ok { ... return cached, nil }` in `getUserPermissions`, and similarly in `getAnonymousPermissions`). Caching is now handled earlier via the new `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` path called from `Check`/`List`, and new tests were added for cache-based `Check`/`List` behavior.
